body:
#AbhijeetDipke’s June 6 Protest: The #CockroachJantaParty Moves Offline

@abhijeet_dipke’s call for supporters to gather on June 6 and demand the resignation of Education Minister @dpradhanbjp marks an important moment in the evolution of the so-called “Cockroach Janta Party” movement. For the first time, a phenomenon that has largely existed online is attempting to test its strength on the streets.

The issues being raised by Dipke and his followers may well be genuine. Concerns about examinations, recruitment processes, transparency and accountability in public institutions resonate with many young Indians. Governments should never dismiss such grievances out of hand.

However, serious questions remain about the movement itself.

The extraordinary growth of the Cockroach Janta Party across social media platforms was anything but ordinary. Its follower counts exploded in a manner that appeared highly unusual and, to many observers, distinctly inorganic. Large numbers of bot-like accounts, coordinated amplification patterns and suspicious engagement metrics across platforms have led to persistent doubts about how much of the movement’s apparent popularity reflects real people rather than digital manipulation.

That does not automatically invalidate every concern raised by its supporters. But it does raise legitimate questions about who is driving the movement, how it achieved such rapid visibility, and whether its online strength accurately reflects real-world public support.

The June 6 protest will therefore be closely watched. Not only will it provide a clearer picture of the movement’s genuine grassroots reach, it will also test whether an online phenomenon can successfully transition into an organised offline force.

Recent developments in several countries across South Asia have demonstrated how digitally mobilised protest movements can quickly escalate beyond their original demands and, in some cases, turn confrontational or violent. For that reason alone, any government would be expected to monitor such gatherings carefully.

The challenge for authorities will be maintaining public order without overreacting. Excessive force or heavy-handed action risks elevating fringe figures into national symbols. At the same time, legitimate concerns about the origins, methods and objectives of the movement cannot simply be ignored.

June 6 may ultimately reveal whether the Cockroach Janta Party is a genuine mass movement, a social media mirage, or something in between. @CJP_2029 @Cockroachisback

A casual tweet. A satirical party name. A million registered members.

What started as a reaction to a controversial remark quickly transformed into one of the most talked-about youth-led political movements in India.

In this conversation, Abhijeet(@abhijeet_dipke) explains how the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) emerged, why it resonated so strongly with Gen Z, and what the movement says about unemployment, accountability, education, and the growing frustration among young Indians.

From applying for jobs in the United States and playing FIFA on a random evening to suddenly becoming the face of a nationwide movement, Abhijeet shares the story behind CJP, the June 6 protest, his vision for political accountability, and why millions of young people feel unheard by mainstream politics.

We also discuss the NEET controversy, education reforms, social media-driven political mobilization, youth participation in democracy, the future of CJP, and whether online outrage can translate into real-world action.

Watch till the end and let us know your views in the comments.

body:
Something doesn't add up.

The Cockroach Janta Party was launched around a specific grievance involving the CJI and the Education Minister. Yet, within weeks, its Chief Spokesperson is talking about entirely different issues:

• Culture of non-answerability
• Not holding press conferences
• Not talking to the media
• Suppression of independent voices

If these are now the central themes, then this movement appears to have evolved far beyond its original stated purpose.

That is precisely what concerns me.

A protest that begins with one issue but quickly shifts into a broader political narrative naturally raises questions about its real objectives. Citizens have every right to protest, but they also have every right to ask: What is the actual agenda here?

The sudden transition from a specific grievance to a full-scale critique of governance deserves scrutiny, not blind applause.

Not taking prior permission for the Jantar Mantar protest is not an oversight. It is the plan. They want Delhi Police to intervene. They want visuals. They want a “crackdown” they can sell to cameras and foreign funders. The script is old. The faces are new.

Now they ask, why do we need permission for a designated protest site? Jantar Mantar is a designated protest site. That is correct. But designated does not mean ungoverned. Even a court is a designated space for justice and you still file a proper petition, follow procedure, and respect the process. A hospital is designated for treatment and you still register before the doctor sees you. Designation means the right is recognised. It does not mean rules disappear.

Permission is not suppression. It is order. And those who resist even that basic step are not protecting your right to protest. They are protecting their right to chaos.

Who exactly are these “angry youths” they keep invoking? Anger is real. Manipulation of that anger is a political industry. Dissent has a constitutional home. It is called the Supreme Court. Use it. But understand this clearly, the ones calling you to the streets will not share your FIR or your ruined career. They will share your photograph.

मुसलमानों !!

6 जून को कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी जंतर मंतर पर प्रोटेस्ट करेगी। मुसलमानों से गुजारिश है कि इस प्रोटेस्ट से दूर रहिएगा, बल्कि उस रास्ते से गुजरने की कोशिश भी मत कीजिएगा। अगर आपका घर उसे जगह के आसपास है तो एक दिन के लिए वह जगह ही छोड़ दीजिए।

100% उस दिन बवाल होगा और  हमेशा की तरह मुसलमान बली का बकरा बनाया जाएगा। बाकी लोग अपने घर चले जाएंगे लेकिन आप खालिद सैफ़ी, मीरान हैदर और उमर खालिद की तरह जेल जाएंगे। आप पर उन सभी धाराओं में मुकदमे दर्ज होंगे जिसमें आप 10 साल तक जेल से बाहर नहीं आ सकेंगे।

body:
My two cents on what's going to happen in Delhi on Saturday, June 6, 2026.

@abhijeet_dipke, the founder of the @Cockroachisback, has announced to land in Delhi at 0800 Hrs that day. It is unlikely that the Modi govt will try to arrest him there, knowing the massive support the CJP is receiving from all sections of society. I'm not expecting a crowd of thousands to reach the airport to receive him. If they do make it there, the Modi govt will try to scatter them under the pretext of airport security issues. NO FORCE WILL BE USED & NO ARRESTS WILL BE MADE AT THE AIRPORT itself, given the heavy presence of foreign visitors and the world's eyes on this protest.

As per the announced plans, the CJP will then head to the Parliament Street PS to seek permission for a protest later that day at Jantar Mantar. Though JM is a designated space for protests and the police should grant permission, knowing Amit Shah well, the Delhi police will likely deny it, citing law & order issues and protocol rules for applying.

This is where story will unfold. The moment this news breaks, the protestors who have started arriving to join the protest, especially the angry students & Gen-Z masses, might sit in protest anyway. This will trigger a clash between the police and the protestors. The govt might use force against them. This is where they might arrest Abhijeet Dipke under the pretext of inciting the crowd to disrupt law & order and creating unrest in the country. The BJP’s pre-prepared toolkit will be launched to defame the CJP as a foreign-funded entity formed to create civil unrest in India. If that happens, the protest will immediately spread across the country and become the most massive movement since Independence.

If the CJP decides to postpone the protest due to the lack of permission, the Modi govt, together with its 'godi media' & IT cell, will start calling it a failed protest and label Dipke and others 'Darpok'. However, whether or not a clash takes place, the Modi govt will be closely gauging the strength of this online satirical party and the support it receives.

It is unlikely that the protest will be allowed to take place smoothly. Instead, there are chances that the govt may take another route by offering to hold a dialogue and giving false assurances, just as they did during the farmers' and the Ladakh protest. It will be interesting to see on what charges and at what stage they will arrest Abhijeet Dipke to weaken the party and the movement. However, this time it is not just Muslims, farmers, defense personnel, or bankers; it is a charged-up Gen-Z. THINGS ARE DEFINITELY NOT GOING TO BE EASY FOR MODI FROM NOW ON.

So, I suggest everyone joining the protest remain calm and not lose their temper. THE WORLD IS WATCHING. Let them use force if they do; it will only strengthen the storm against this autocratic, shameless govt. To everyone else, whether you are a student, Gen-Z, or a parent; Hindu or Muslim; rich or poor; upper or lower caste; irrespective of your skin color, what you eat, what you wear, or what language you speak, HIT THE ROADS AND JOIN THE MOVEMENT. Those serving as honest bureaucrats, police, and defense forces should also join the protest for the sake of their future generations. If you think the CJP is a fraud, join the protests organized by the Congress party. If you have ideological differences with Congress, join whichever party you support, but protest against this govt. Remember, this is about your future and the future of coming generations.

I'm sure you have read about Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement against the British. There can't be a better way to show a common man's strength to this autocratic, shameless, and failed govt than by protesting and joining a similar non-cooperative movement.

This govt doesn't want you to ask questions; they don't want to be accountable; they don't want you to look them in the eye.

The life of this parrot is only in its eyes. Look into their eyes and ask questions.

Protest at Jantar Mantar 

 Delhi Police on High Alert Over Cockroach Janata Party Protest Call

▪️ Delhi Police has intensified security arrangements ahead of the protest call given by the Cockroach Janata Party.

▪️ Authorities are also focusing on ensuring that commuters and the general public face minimal inconvenience.

▪️ Extensive barricading has been put in place on key routes leading to New Delhi.

▪️ Police personnel have been deployed on all roads connecting Nizamuddin to Parliament Street, with heightened vigilance across the South-East district.

▪️ Prohibitory orders under Section 163 have been imposed in sensitive areas.

▪️ Special deployment has been made around Nizamuddin, a key connectivity point for Haryana and Faridabad, to prevent any unauthorized movement.

▪️ Police sources said strict action will be taken against any suspicious activity or movement.Source-based report from police inputs.

The Cockroach Janta party is a bit like a temperature check that has quantified public anger against Modi government.

It was traditionally the job of the media to echo public sentiment. But they're now in the business of criminalising dissent.

At a time political opposition has been systematically weakened, media is bought and institutions are compromised, it is quite creditable to mount a protest in any form.

The CJP has rallied around an extremely important issue of educational corruption, which concerns a range of young people in India.

Many common people that I've spoken to are kinda surprised with the response to CJP but it has also emboldened them to express dissent.

And that counts for something.

2,600 unemployed youths, all supporters of the CJP, protesting for job regularisation and opposing amendments to recruitment rules.

Abhijeet Dipke : We demand the resignation of PM Modi. Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, the Union Minister of Labour and Employment should resign with immediate effect.

Saurav Ass... sorry, Dass : We stand with the protesters. Even if they did not obtain prior permission from the police, I see no reason why their demands should not be fulfilled.

Ashutosh Ranka : Where are the constitutional and democratic rights of the youth of India ? Modi must resign.

Reporter : Excuse me.......

Sonam Wangchuk : I will begin an indefinite hunger strike and continue protesting against this insensitive government until the demands of the youth are met.

Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, and Sanjay Singh : We challenge the government at the Centre. You dare not stop this protest.

Reporter : Excuse me, sir. This particular protest was led by 2600 unemployed youths of Punjab at the PSPCL headquarters in Patiala. They were lathi charged and beaten with batons by the Punjab Police because they were protesting for jobs in your AAP ruled state.

A deep silence follows.
Abhijeet Dipke: Mmpfff !! I have to board my flight ...
Sonam Wangchuk : Err......I just remembered that I have to catch an Uber to Jantar Mantar.
Ashutosh Ranka : I better prepare for another press conference.
Kejriwal, Sisodia, and others: This is a conspiracy by the BJP and Modi to defame us !!

After 2 minutes.....the protectors and upholders of constitution and democracy and the party showing solidarity with the unemployed youth of India has scurried into their drains and garbage dumps ....at the mention of the word Punjab.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke arrives in Delhi, on his way to Jantar Mantar, he urges Cockroaches for peaceful protest.

He urged supporters to maintain discipline and ensure that the protest remains peaceful. Hundreds of CJP supporters were gathered at airport, to receive him.

Security beefed up at Jantar Mantar ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party protest.

⭐Cockroach Janta Party Storms Jantar Mantar — June 6, 2026⭐

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), landed in Delhi early Saturday morning and headed straight to Parliament Street Police Station to seek protest permission. Police granted permission and the demonstration at Jantar Mantar began shortly after.

Thousands of young supporters gathered at the iconic protest site, carrying national flags and books, demanding the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over repeated paper leaks in NEET-UG, CUET, SSC GD and CBSE examinations.

Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk also joined the protest, stating — "If not us, who? If not now, when?"

Heavy security was deployed across the area. Several students alleged that police pressured them not to attend, though authorities denied the claims.

The CJP movement was born on May 16, 2026, after India's Chief Justice compared unemployed youth to "cockroaches and parasites." Within days, the movement exploded to over 20 million Instagram followers — turning an insult into a revolution.

Today, that online revolution hit the streets.

It's a wakeup call for those in power.. 🇮🇳

The protest at Jantar Mantar by CJP will reach far beyond the people on ground. Crores of netizens will receive and react to reels and posts from Jantar Mantar.

The BJP continues to stay in a state of denial. But Gen Z is now actively seeking change. It would be a great mistake from the thinktank of BJP to brush this aside. 

The core feeling and that disenchantment behind this whole movement is very telling. The youth is up against the system that has been denying them jobs, quality education and a voice. 

If not today, then tomorrow. This same Gen Z will put an end to the politics of hate. It would call out inefficiency in governance and seek better and educated leaders to run the country... leaders that talk about education, healthcare and basics, leaders who know how to live up to their promises.

It's only a matter of time.

Shivsena Party chief Shri Uddhav Thackeray has issued the following statement regarding the agitation by the youths in Delhi:

“An agitation of ‘Cockroaches’ has begun at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.
Those whom we call the destiny-makers and future of the country — thousands of young people — have come out on the streets in the scorching heat, carrying their pain and worries about their future.
It is not right to belittle them by calling them ‘cockroaches’ and deny them justice.
The NEET paper leak has devastated lakhs of young people. All these aggrieved young men and women are now raising their voices by becoming cockroaches.
The government will have to listen to their demands.
Do not underestimate the cockroaches — this is the warning given by the agitation at Jantar Mantar!”

ONE DEMAND: RESIGNATION.
We were on the ground at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi today as Abhijeet Dipke , founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), addressed hundreds of student protestors and the media. The message from the crowd was unified: Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan must step down. Following widespread outrage over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal, disruptions in the CUET and SSC GD exams, and grading discrepancies within the CBSE Class 12 evaluation system.  The demonstration marks the first major offline mobilization for the CJP—a youth-led movement formed after a controversial courtroom remark by CJI Surya Kant comparing certain youth activists to "cockroaches and parasites." To reclaim the phrase, many students arrived today wearing cockroach masks and holding flowers, demanding systemic accountability for over 1 crore affected students nationwide.

body:
'Deep State' Dipke's Cockroach Protest Stands 
Exposed; Leftist Roaches Crawl Over Jantar Mantar

Roaches roasting under Delhi’s baking sun were roaring one line today — "Cockroaches never fear, never die."

That part is true. But there’s something else about cockroaches they’re not telling you.

Did you know a cockroach can survive without its head? Cut the head off, and it keeps walking for days — on pure instinct. It can’t eat. It can’t think. It just… keeps moving until it starves or rots from the inside.

That is exactly what we are watching today.

June 6, 2026. Jantar Mantar — that sacred feeding ground where India’s professional protestors have dined for decades. 

The Cockroach Janata Party had promised a mega youth revolution. NEET leaks. Exam scams. Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. Twenty-two million algorithm-engineered bots screaming fire across Instagram and X.

The Roach in Chief himself — Abhijeet Dipke — landed fresh off a flight from Boston, constitution in one hand, promises of flowers for the police in the other. They said the streets would burn. 

They said Gen-Z would rise. What actually showed up? A few hundred cockroaches at best. Not even two thousand. Outnumbered by Delhi Police and the bored media crew waiting for a spectacle that never arrived. 

The same old headless wonders – Samajwadi remnants, RJD ruffians, Congress leftovers, AAPtards, and the usual left radicals – are twitching their antennae, desperately sniffing for any scent of chaos.

These political cockroaches had their heads severed in 2014. Electoral heads. Power heads. The constitutional route to power was shut for them — not by any conspiracy, but by the repeated verdict of the Indian people. 

More than a decade out of power with zero realistic hope of returning through the ballot box. So what do they do? They keep twitching. 

They keep marching. They try to reattach their severed heads by plugging into fresh student anger — NEET leaks, exam scams, anything that hurts young people — and then coating that genuine grievance with the same old anarchist poison.

This is not new. This is the exact same script we saw in anti-CAA. The exact same script we saw in the farmers’ protest. Manufacture outrage, import professional andolanjeevis from SFI, AISA, and AISF, bring in the Dafli Gang to beat Umar Khalid-style rhythms, and then pray that the resulting chaos becomes so big that the constitutional order cracks. 

If you cannot win elections, trigger enough street fire that you can usurp power through the back door — exactly as their foreign masters and deep-state scriptwriters have taught them for years.

That is why Abhijeet Dipke flies in from Boston. That is why the same discredited AAPiyas suddenly discover “student outrage". 

That is why Sauraav Das, their spokesperson, lasts ten minutes in the Delhi sun before retreating under a tree with cold coffee in his hand – while still demanding the prime minister's resignation. 

These are not revolutionaries. These are parasites who cannot stand the heat of real sunlight or real accountability.

They keep saying, “We are not a planned party. This is pure students’ outrage.” But the moment the Dafli starts and the old slogans return, the mask slips. 

The same people who spent ten years crying only about Hindu-Muslim politics are now trying to turn every exam paper leak into a constitutional crisis. The hypocrisy is not even clever anymore. It is just pathetic.

And the youth? The real Gen-Z and millennials? They stayed home. Because twenty-two million followers were mostly bots. 

Because the people leading this circus have been discredited so many times that even teenagers can smell the rot. The real students of this country are busy preparing for the next exam, building their futures, and watching India rise — not waiting to be extras in someone else’s failed revolution.

Real accountability on NEET and exam leaks is necessary. Absolutely. But turning every grievance into another prolonged dharna to topple a democratically elected government? The people have seen this movie too many times. They are not buying tickets anymore.

The cockroaches will keep bumbling. They will survive the head cut for a few more days — maybe weeks. They will keep twitching on pure instinct, hoping the next manufactured outrage finally gives them the chaos they need. 

But without real public backing, without electoral legitimacy, without a head – starvation is inevitable. Infection has already begun.

This civilisational nation is not going to let a handful of scurrying roaches feast on manufactured outrage and turn it into unconstitutional anarchy. 

History has it: India does not rise on wishful anarchy. It never will.

The headless march has already begun to die. We are just watching the slow, inevitable end.

These political cockroaches had their heads severed in 2014. Electoral heads. Power heads. The constitutional route to power was shut for them — not by any conspiracy, but by the repeated verdict of the Indian people. More than a decade out of power with zero realistic hope of returning through the ballot box. So what do they do? They keep twitching. They keep marching. They try to reattach their severed heads by plugging into fresh student anger — NEET leaks, exam scams, anything that hurts young people — and then coating that genuine grievance with the same old anarchist poison. This is not new. This is the exact same script we saw in anti-CAA. The exact same script we saw in the farmers’ protest. Manufacture outrage, import professional andolanjeevis from SFI, AISA, and AISF, bring in the Dafli Gang to beat Umar Khalid-style rhythms, and then pray that the resulting chaos becomes so big that the constitutional order cracks. If you cannot win elections, trigger enough street fire that you can usurp power through the back door — exactly as their foreign masters and deep-state scriptwriters have taught them for years. This is pure students’ outrage.” But the moment the Dafli starts and the old slogans return, the mask slips. The same people who spent ten years crying only about Hindu-Muslim politics are now trying to turn every exam paper leak into a constitutional crisis. The hypocrisy is not even clever anymore. Real accountability on NEET and exam leaks is necessary. Absolutely. But turning every grievance into another prolonged dharna to topple a democratically elected government? The people have seen this movie too many times. They are not buying tickets anymore. The cockroaches will keep bumbling. They will survive the head cut for a few more days — maybe weeks. They will keep twitching on pure instinct, hoping the next manufactured outrage finally gives them the chaos they need. This civilisational nation is not going to let a handful of scurrying roaches feast on manufactured outrage and turn it into unconstitutional anarchy. History has it: India does not rise on wishful anarchy. It never will. The headless march has already begun to die. We are just watching the slow, inevitable end. body:
History bears witness to the fact that those in power dread nothing more than individuals who ask questions without waving a political flag.

Today, the very youth who ask these uncomfortable questions have taken to the streets. Gathered at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, these young minds are contemptuously being labeled as "TILCHATTE" by some, who are even callously talking about spraying HIT on them.

While the BJP’s frustration is understandable, why the hell are these Congressmen losing their minds and overstepping their bounds? The very youth you are abusing have held up a mirror today to the ruling party, the opposition, and the media alike.
 * **No political stage,**
 * **No constellation of big-shot leaders,**
 * **No electoral rallies,**
 * **No crowds herded into hired buses.**
Yet, thousands of youngsters stood their ground. Most of them were likely sitting on a scorching road, under a blazing sun, without fans or tents, enduring conditions like a furnace for the very first time in their lives.

Those who are undermining them or mocking them are not just insulting these protestors, they are mocking the entire Gen Z and the younger generation of this nation.

These are the very youth who have been raising their voices for years against **unemployment, paper leaks, recruitment scams, inflation, and a compromised media**. Yet, in response, they are mockingly branded as "TILCHATTE."

If this youth quietly tolerates everything, they are hailed as the "future of the nation," but the moment they demand accountability, they are reduced to pests.

When Sonam Wangchuk arrived at the venue, people immediately began painting him as the "New Anna Hazare." Such comparisons are merely a testament to their desperation. Even the Congress is mocking Sonam Wangchuk. They evidently have no respect even for those whom the Modi government jailed simply for speaking up for the betterment of this country.

Some are dismissing this gathering of young citizens as a mere "bubble," claiming that barely 100 to 200 people showed up. To those skeptics, let me say this: deny it all you want, but you cannot escape the reality that this is the boiling wrath of the youth. The anger was always there. Today, it simply erupted and found expression.

Even if it is a passing bubble, the youth desperately need a platform. Their rage and resistance should not be measured by mere headcount, but understood through the depth of their anguish.

The voice that echoed at Jantar Mantar today is not just a protest; it is the restlessness of a generation that no longer wants rhetoric, it demands answers.

Dismissing lakhs of young citizens of this country as "cockroaches" will not make the problems vanish. However, it *will* definitively prove that the establishment has absolutely no answers to their questions.
**Keep questioning.**
**Keep demanding answers.**

Because in a true democracy, a citizen’s greatest weapon will always be their voice.

body:
Thousands of students descended on New Delhi's Jantar Mantar under the banner of the "Cockroach Janta Party", a satirical youth movement that reclaimed a term India's Chief Justice reportedly used to dismiss unemployed young people, and turned it into a rallying cry against the country's broken exam system.

The movement, founded by 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, has amassed 22 million Instagram followers and 800,000 signatures demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. 

The immediate trigger: the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam paper leak, affecting over 10 million students.

Protesters wore cockroach masks and carried placards reading "Cockroaches do not die."  https://t.co/pa4tklIPA5

कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी का सुप्रीम लीडर अभिजीत दीपके अपने शानदार भाषण में कहा, जब वो भारत आ रहा था 

तब उसकी माँ और बहन बहुत रो रही थी उन्हें लग रहा था यहां आते ही सरकार गिरफ्तार करवा देगी.

इसके बाद अभिजीत दीपके ने दमदार नारा दिया, 

• सरकार की तानाशाही नही चलेगी नही चलेगी.
• नही डरेंगे नही डरेंगे. 
• धर्म की राजनीति बंद करो, बंद करो

भीड़ से एक लड़की ने जोर से चिल्लाकर कहा, जातिवाद बंद करो, बंद करो. अभिजीत दीपके ने इस नारे को नजरअंदाज कर दिया.

सरकार को अभिजीत दीपके और कॉकरोच मूवमेंट से कोई खतरा नही है. इसी कारण आंदोलन की परमिशन मिली, पुलिस एस्कॉर्ट मिला.

कॉकरोच मूवमेंट से सबसे ज्यादा नुकसान कांग्रेस पार्टी को है. राहुल गांधी NEET पेपर लीक और CBSE को बड़ा मुद्दा बना रहे थे. इसी बीच कॉकरोच की तादाद बढ़ जाती है. कॉकरोच मूवमेंट का मूल अर्थ है राहुल गांधी ने अब तक जो किया वो नाकाफी है, वो अक्षम है.

I want to thank each and every one of you who braved the hot summer sun, young kids and students included, and proved that a peaceful protest is our greatest strength. The government cannot touch a unified, peaceful movement. Us cockroaches don’t ever need to fear them.

But this doesn't end here. Dharmendra Pradhan has wronged an entire generation. If he is not removed or does not step down within the next 7 days, we will be forced to continue our protest on the ground.

I will address you all on an Instagram live later today. Stay tuned.

Yesterday (June 6, 2026), the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)- a satirical Gen Z-led online movement turned the youth protest group- held its first major offline demonstration at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.

Led by founder 𝗔𝗯𝗵𝗶𝗷𝗲𝗲𝘁 𝗗𝗶𝗽𝗸𝗲 (who flew in from the US). 
Activist 𝗦𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗺 𝗪𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗰𝗵𝘂𝗸 joined.

𝗣𝘂𝗿𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: Demanding the resignation of 𝘜𝘯𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘌𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘔𝘪𝘯𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘿𝙝𝙖𝙧𝙢𝙚𝙣𝙙𝙧𝙖 𝙋𝙧𝙖𝙙𝙝𝙖𝙣 over alleged irregularities in exams, including the 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗧-𝗨𝗚 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗽𝗮𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗸 (which led to the exam being canceled for ~2.2 million students) and issues with CBSE’s On-Screen Marking system.

Ritika Chandola Reached Jantar Mantar As An Unknown Cockroach In The CJP Protest And Exposed The Topi Media

What was the real motive behind the so-called Gen-Z protest? 

How did the Cockroach Janta Party's demonstration end up becoming little more than a hub for engagement farming? 

To find out, Ritika Chandola reached Jantar Mantar wearing a CJP mask herself. She interacted with several media channels, but the TRP-hungry "cap media" never even bothered to ask who was hiding behind the mask. Their only concern was that someone was speaking against the government something that conveniently fit their narrative. 

It didn't matter who was speaking; what mattered was that the Modi government was being criticized. The media showed little interest in students' concerns or the issues affecting young people. Their focus remained firmly on pushing their own agenda. In this video, discover what Ritika Chandola witnessed firsthand while posing as "Diksha" behind the cockroach mask.
Credit : OpIndia.

Double Standards in Handling Youth Protests?

In Patiala, Punjab (AAP-ruled): Unemployed ITI apprentice linemen (2600 Apprentice Lineman Union) were peacefully demanding jobs after apprenticeship. They sat outside PSPCL HQ for days. Police responded with lathi charge – youths injured (one reportedly lost an eye), 10+ detained, 160+ booked. All for seeking regular employment. https://t.co/oG5uWnTjYa 

Just days later in Delhi (BJP-ruled): #CJP (Cockroach Janata Party) protest at Jantar Mantar – massive youth turnout against NEET/CBSE paper leaks, demanding minister’s resignation. Some raised controversial/“anti-national” slogans, called for chaos in prep, yet Delhi Police granted permission, protest stayed peaceful, no lathi charge, no major crackdown. https://t.co/2uaUKYXyQd
 
Same country. Same youth frustration over jobs & future.
Different ruling parties → Different police response.

Why the selective silence from “youth activists” & big media on Punjab? Because the narrative doesn’t fit when it’s #AAP in power?
Unemployed youth deserve dialogue, not batons – regardless of state. Hypocrisy exposes the politics over people.

Meet Ujjwal 🌻

• You may have already seen him online being trolled and targeted with derogatory slurs like Meetha, Chakka, Hijda, and worse.

• Ujjwal is a 19-year-old queer person who has just passed his Class 12 exams.

• He may have no connection whatsoever to the NEET paper leak controversy, yet he still showed up at the Jantar Mantar protest organized by the Cockroach Janta Party.

• He understands the pain and frustration of the 22 lakh students and their families affected by the paper leak, as well as the millions of others who have suffered because of more than 89 major exam paper leaks across the country.

• As a queer individual fighting for his rights, visibility, and existence in a deeply transphobic and homophobic Indian society, he has likely faced immense struggles himself. Yet despite that, he chose to show up for others.

• He may have participated in protests before too, something that many educated and socially aware people never do in their entire lives.

• From these videos, one thing is clear: he has a great sense of style and carries himself with confidence.

• He is socially aware, respectful, politically conscious, and unafraid to speak about rights, justice, and issues that matter.

• Meanwhile, lowlifes hiding behind fake profiles chose to mock and ridicule him for doing something I would call an act of genuine courage.

• He is far better than the self-proclaimed internet sigmas, alphas, and low-testosterone junglees who are just a burden on society, freeloading on government freebies and spreading hatred online. They are the reason for India's bad reputation globally, not someone like Ujjwal.

• If we had more Ujjwal, people who are aware, confident, educated, and bold enough to challenge a corrupt system. We might have saved thousands of students, women, farmers, LGBTQIA+ people, soldiers, and countless others who lost their lives while fighting for justice.

• And Ujjwal, if you're reading this: we see you. We appreciate you. We love you.

Thank you for showing up when it mattered.

Sending hugs. 🫂❤️

P.S. I apologize for any accidental misgendering or for using incorrect pronouns while referring to him.

दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर 6 जून को कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के प्रदर्शन में शामिल हुई रोहतक के एक स्कूल की महिला गेस्ट टीचर सुलेखा दलाल को विभाग ने निलंबित कर दिया है। 

हालांकि आदेश पत्र में निलंबन का कारण नहीं लिखा है, लेकिन इस प्रदर्शन के अगले ही दिन उनसे फोन पर जवाब भी मांगा गया था।

ऐसे में निलंबन को इसी मामले से जोड़कर देखा जा रहा है। इधर, बहादुरगढ़ के सेक्टर-9 में रह रही शिक्षिका सुलेखा ने कहा कि कारण तो विभाग जाने, मगर पेपर लीक मामला उनके बेटे और युवाओं के भविष्य से जुड़ा विषय है। इस पर वे हार नहीं मानेंगी, चाहे कुछ भी हो जाए।

सुलेखा दलाल मूल रूप से बहादुरगढ़ के मेहंदीपुर डाबौदा से हैं और रोहतक के रैनकपुरा स्थित राजकीय मिडिल स्कूल में गेस्ट टीचर हैं। राजनीति से लेकर भजन गायन और सोशल मीडिया पर रील बनाने में भी सक्रिय रहती हैं।

रोहतक डीईईओ की ओर से उनके निलंबन आदेश जारी कर बीईओ ऑफिस हेडक्वार्टर तय किया है। बिना अनुमति हेडक्वार्टर न छोड़ने के आदेश हैं। 

इधर, शिक्षिका सुलेखा दलाल ने कहा कि पेपर लीक से उनके बेटे को भी परेशानी हुई है। मगर यह केवल मेरे बेटे नहीं बल्कि लाखों युवाओं से जुड़ा मामला है। इसमें आखिर तक लड़ाई लड़ेंगी।

Thousands of participants from across India have gathered at Savitribai Phule Pune University in Pune for a massive protest led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), founded by Abhijeet Dipke. The nationwide agitation targets repeated irregularities in CBSE and NEET examinations, with CJP demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak and CBSE OSM exam evaluation controversy. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk and hundreds of students are among those expected to participate. The protest, beginning at 4 PM on the SPPU campus, will later expand to major cities including Lucknow, Amritsar, Bengaluru, Jaipur, and Hyderabad. From June 20, an indefinite sit-in protest will be held at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi until Pradhan steps down.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) says it is an organic, non partisan movement fighting bad governance.

Then here is a simple question:

Will CJP speak on Punjab?

Under the AAP government, Punjab's debt has crossed ₹4 lakh crore. Opposition leaders cite 587+ overdose deaths, 306 illegal mining cases, rising gangster activity and worsening law and order. Farmer protests against the land pooling policy have also intensified.

If CJP can question every other government, can it question Bhagwant Mann too?

Do you believe Punjab is being governed well?
Do these numbers concern you?
And most importantly, should Bhagwant Mann resign and take responsibility if these failures are real?
A movement that claims to be above politics must be willing to hold every government accountable, not just the governments it dislikes.

यह तरकीब पुरानी है, जिसे अब जनता और विपक्षी दल दोनों अच्छे से समझते हैं।

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) was manhandled and slapped multiple times during a youth protest in Jaipur today.

> While arriving at the Shaheed Smarak protest site and being carried on supporters’ shoulders

> Dipke was confronted by a small group of men in the crowd before he could speak

> He was manhandled, his scarf pulled, and slapped several times amid the chaos

> Videos of the scuffle show him urging calm and non-violence

> He said, “No matter how many slaps we have to face, we will not resort to violence” and described the attack as a “diversion tactic” from their core demands

> Police detained at least two youths involved in the assault. The protest continued peacefully afterward.

The gathering focused on NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks, unemployment, education system failures

> Demands for systemic reforms including the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), transformed online outrage into a massive physical demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar today. Led by founder Abhijeet Dipke, hundreds of students and youth gathered to launch an indefinite protest demanding the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET-UG exam irregularities and paper leaks. In a striking move reminiscent of pandemic-era gestures, protesters banged thalis (plates) with spoons, chanting "Go Pradhan Go" to demand accountability from the central government.

So, Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, has called for an indefinite protest until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns. However, the police have already denied permission for the protest. This may not end well for Abhijeet and the CJP. He has also called on people to gather there in large numbers.

How will this end? Quite simply:

Since the police have denied permission, events may unfold similarly to what happened during the SSC protests. Late at night, or at a time when very few people remain, the police may ask most protesters to go home. Vendors and people running stalls in the area may also be told to leave. Once a large portion of the crowd has dispersed, the electricity could be cut off. Then, Delhi police constables who are already present within the crowd may try to create confusion and disorder and will start beating people. People could be pushed off the stage, and some may be beaten or severely injured during the chaos. After that, the Delhi Police may conduct a lathi charge, and Abhijeet along with some of his associates could be arrested. That is how the protest may ultimately come to an end.

🤯 BIG | Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke leads his party to a massive protest on Day-3 at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

Seems like the Cockroach Janta Party’s drama has been hijacked by this Harsh fellow today. People are making videos about him, taking his bites, and giving him all the attention. Bro is having the time of his life. Why should Dipke and the boys have all the fun? Lmao.

But bro flips. Earlier, he was making video after video praising CJP, showing up less as a reporter and more as a supporter. Then bro got ambitious and started thinking he was one of the leaders. He challenged Dipke, got taken into custody by the Delhi Police, was released, and then went right back to Jantar Mantar, featuring in videos from outside. What a sequence.

Also, the coordination between CJP and the Delhi Police almost deserves an award. First, he gets detained because CJP wants him removed from the site. Then he gets released at the request of one of its spokespersons. Wow. Wish the Delhi Police were this helpful to ordinary citizens as well.

Now the spotlight has shifted, at least for the day. It’s funny, but it’s also a circus. That’s what happens when a movement built around a legitimate cause is led by opportunists with a constantly shifting, pendulum-like ideology. Personal ambitions start taking over, everyone wants a bigger role, and the cause itself slowly becomes secondary to the drama.

@CJP_for_India

body:
सत्ता के अहंकार में डूबी मोदी सरकार अब इस मुकाम पर पहुँच गई है कि अपने अधिकारों, निष्पक्ष परीक्षाओं और सुरक्षित भविष्य की मांग करने वाले छात्रों को ही शिक्षा मंत्री “आतंकवादी” कह रहे हैं।

ज़रा सोचिए - जिसकी नाकामी से इतने पेपर लीक हुए, जिसके राज में 20 बच्चों ने जान दे दी, जिसने करोड़ों युवाओं का भविष्य अंधेरे में धकेल दिया - वो आज पीड़ित बच्चों और उनकी आवाज़ उठाने वालों को “दहशतगर्द” बता रहा है। 

पर यह कोई नई बात नहीं: अन्नदाता किसानों को "आंदोलनजीवी और परजीवी" कहा। सवाल पूछने वाले को “Anti-National” कहा। और अब युवाओं को “दहशतगर्द।”

जो भी सरकार से सवाल पूछे - उसे देशद्रोही बता दो, यही इनकी पूरी राजनीति है।

धर्मेंद्र प्रधान जी, देश के करोड़ों युवाओं से तुरंत माफ़ी माँगिए और अपनी नाकामियों के लिए इस्तीफ़ा दीजिए।

और रही मेरी बात - आप मुझ पर जितने चाहें हमले कर लीजिए। मैंने कोटा में कहा था, और फिर कहता हूँ: यह शिक्षा व्यवस्था आज सिर्फ़ एक वसूली तंत्र बन गई है। मैं इसे ऐसे ही नहीं रहने दूँगा।

हर बच्चे को सस्ती, अच्छी शिक्षा और निष्पक्ष परीक्षा मिले - इस आवाज़ को उठाना मैं कभी बंद नहीं करूँगा।

8 days of the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar have now been completed.

There are around 150 people present throughout the day (including YouTubers), but around 300 people show up during meal times.

Approximate daily food & refreshments:

-Breakfast: ₹100 × 300 = ₹30,000
-Lunch: ₹200 × 300 = ₹60,000
-Evening Snacks: ₹100 × 300 = ₹30,000
-Dinner: ₹200 × 300 = ₹60,000
-Fruits, Frooti & other snacks: ₹100 × 300 = ₹30,000

Food & refreshments total: ₹2,10,000/day

Other daily expenses:

-Tent & Stage: ₹3,000/day
-Mic & Sound System: ₹2,000/day
-Washroom Cleaning: ₹1,500/day
-Student Union: ₹200 × 150 = ₹30,000/day
-Drinking Water: 150 people × 5 bottles = 750 bottles × ₹20 = ₹15,000/day
-Cigarettes: ₹3,000/day

Other expenses total: ₹54,500/day

Estimated total per day: ₹2,64,500

Estimated total for 8 days: ₹21,16,000

As per sources, Mohammad Junaid runs a mobile repair shop, and Sardar Ji runs a catering service.

Can Junaid and Sardar really afford to spend over ₹21 lakh on their own?

जिस आदमी ने इसे बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर बताया, वह अब हंस रहा है और उन मुट्ठी भर 10-20 सच्चे प्रोटेस्टर्स का खुलेआम मज़ाक उड़ा रहा है जो असल में जंतर-मंतर पर आए थे। जो एक तथाकथित आंदोलन के तौर पर शुरू हुआ था, वह उन्हीं लोगों की कीमत पर मज़ाक बन गया है जिन्होंने इसे सीरियसली लिया था।

असली कमिटमेंट ऑनलाइन शोर से नहीं मापा जाता - यह उन लोगों से पता चलता है जो गर्मी में पक्के इरादे के साथ खड़े रहते हैं, भले ही संख्या कम हो। दोगलापन सामने आ गया।

#अभिजीतदीपके #जंतरमंतर #प्रोटेस्टरियलिटी ....

One Minute Silence for those who genuinely believed Abhijit Dipke was serious about the protest.

The man who hyped it up is now laughing and openly mocking the handful of 10-20 sincere protestors who actually showed up at Jantar Mantar. What started as a supposed movement has turned into a joke at the expense of the very people who took it seriously.

Real commitment isn't measured by online noise - it's shown by those who stand in the heat with conviction, even when numbers are low. Hypocrisy exposed.

**Facts on Sonam Wangchuk hunger strike at Jantar Mantar:**

- Wangchuk began an **indefinite hunger strike** today (28 June 2026) at Jantar Mantar, joining the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest over exam irregularities (e.g. NEET) and demanding accountability from Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

- CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleges Delhi Police cut water/sanitation after the strike started, public toilets have no water, and a portable toilet was denied despite health concerns for Wangchuk.

- **Delhi Police denial** (DCP New Delhi official tweet): The allegations are “falsehoods and misinformation.” Police have **no role** in providing or maintaining water or sanitation facilities at the site.

Public toilets and civic amenities at Jantar Mantar fall under municipal bodies (MCD), not Delhi Police. The CJP protest has run since 20 June with occasional prior facility complaints.

No independent confirmation of deliberate police cutoff today. This is allegation vs official denial.

Parents who have lost their children to institutional murd3r are at Jantar Mantar right now. More than 10 people are doing a hunger strike. 

You may have differences with the politics of some of the leaders of CJP, I know I do. But how do I look into the eyes of a father who has lost his 9 year old to bullying, and is at the protest site simply for the sake of the idea of justice? How do I deny the pain of a mother who has carried her 17 year old daughter's photograph to the site because her daughter is dead? How do I not stand with the father whose son, even after death has been equated to a terrorist?

I don't know where this protest is going, or if it will achieve anything. But I will be politically dishonest if I don't stand with people who have lost their children to the abject incompetence of this BJP government, despite my differences with certain spokespersons' transphobic and misogynistic stances. 

In solidarity with all at Jantar Mantar. In solidarity with the hunger striking students and activists.

They expressed their whole-hearted support for the movement and assured the students and youth that the CPI(M) will stand with them in their fight for justice.

राहुल गांधी और NSUI नीट पेपर लीक पर बीजेपी सरकार को घेर रहे थे.

अरविंद केजरीवाल, अखिलेश यादव, ममता बनर्जी और अन्य विपक्षी पार्टियां भी पेपर लीक मुद्दे पर आंदोलन कर रही थीं.

पकी पकाई फसल बीच में कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी खाने आ गयी. विपक्षी पार्टियों के समर्थकों के बीच ऐसा संगठन है जो विपक्ष नेताओं के खिलाफ है.

कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी के नेता अभिजीत दीपके बीजेपी सरकार के खिलाफ उतना मुखर नही हैं जितना होना चाहिए. अगर कल को कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी राजनीति में आती है तो नुकसान विपक्षी पार्टियों को ही होगा. बीजेपी इसी कारण इस आंदोलन को कुचल नही रही है.

Looks like the alleged rumours about #Wangchuk may be right.
Leaders from Ladakh showed little support to Wangchuk since they felt that their issues wrt Ladakh were in discussion with the Centre since long and close to some, if not complete solution.. Challenging the govt now did little to help their cause. 
 
A reluctant #Sonam disappointed with the support, not just at Jantar Mantar but even from Ladakh leaders, is visibly having issues with #Dipke and gang for changing the mood of the protest from - requesting to warning to abusing to manipulating to now turning it visibly political. Also, Dipke and others abandoning wangchuk for hours in the name of meetings, keeping him in the dark and sudden appearances of political leaders on stage without consulting with him has made Wangchuk realise that the protest is not serving his purpose or helping his image.

In all likelihood, wangchuk will pull the plug off his contribution to this naatak mandli very soon in the coming days.
 
There are a lot of cold exchanges happening behind the curtains... The lack of seriousness of the protestors who are more bothered about 'khane mein kya hai' than any concrete cause has also pissed Sonam off. 
He gave a call to #CJP supporters to send recorded videos of 1 day of annshann from home to show support to their #hungerktrike ... Not one came. The disinterest is evident.  

"Yeh hai badlav ka chehra? Khane peene gaane se aage koi kuch karna nahi chahta. Kab tak buffet laga lagakar motivate karenge inhe. Sab pointless hai ." - guess who said that.

Those Protesting Against NEET Paper Leak Make A Website Which Then Gets Compromised, Personal Details Of Volunteers Leaked : 
The Joke That Is CJP

The Cockroach Janta Party, founded by Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) member Abhijeet Dipke, has compromised the sensitive personal information of people who were misled into believing that he was fighting for the cause of ‘students’ in the aftermath of the NEET paper leak.

For the unversed, Dipke had called upon his followers to register on his party’s website :
https://t.co/KlVSTjKcp6
soon after it was launched.

Later, the AAP member alleged that the government took down his website, a claim that was later found to be false. It has now come to light that the users who trusted Abhijeet Dipke with their personal information have now been left vulnerable at the hands of potential cybercriminals.

On Wednesday (1st July), OSINT expert Nisarga took to X (formerly Twitter) to expose vulnerabilities on the website of the Cockroach Janta Party.

A major scene unfolded at the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar today during dinner.

People were served roti with khichdi, and many got upset, asking, "What kind of combination is this?"

They were almost about to get into a physical confrontation with Junaid. But at the last moment, some CJP members stepped in and apologized, assuring everyone that it wouldn't happen again from tomorrow.

Only then did the crowd calm down. They gave a final warning that they wanted a better dinner from the next day, and only then did they somehow finish their khichdi and roti.

Just look at the food tantrums at a protest. 😭

The only person missing was the government.

Students are still firm on one demand: Dharmendra Pradhan must resign.

In solidarity with Sonam Wangchuk ji's @wangchuk66
courageous hunger strike for accountability in India's broken education system, 

I will observe a full 1-day fast today (July 6th).

While @Wangchuk66 health weakens day after day at Jantar Mantar, the BJP government remains stone deaf. 

At least 14-20 young NEET aspirants have died by suicide amid the pain, uncertainty, and despair caused by the paper leak scandal — bright futures snuffed out by systemic failure and callous negligence. 

CJP's determined protest at Jantar Mantar has now stretched into its second week+ (with Wangchuk on Day 9 of his fast), yet the Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan still clings to his chair.

 Opposition parties and notable voices have extended support, but the government offers only silence. 

Enough is enough. 

These deaths are not "statistics" - they are our children, our dreams, our nation's tomorrow. 

We demand the immediate resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. 

Fix the system. Deliver justice. Or step aside. 

#PradhanGoBack

Latest Guardian Sob Story On Umar Khalid Is Another Indication That NEET Is Just A Mask

On 30th June, The Guardian published a sympathetic profile of Umar Khalid, presenting the accused in the larger conspiracy case related to the 2020 anti-Hindu Delhi Riots as one of India’s most prominent “political prisoners” and a victim of a government crackdown on dissent. Built around reflections on prison, fading hope, Dostoevsky and Bhagat Singh, the article largely avoided examining the prosecution’s case against him.

The article needs to be scrutinised not just for what it said, but also for what it deliberately left outside the frame. The publication came amid open support for Khalid from the leadership and supporters of the so-called Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), whose protests were launched around the NEET paper leak and youth issues. However, protesters and CJP supporters, both online and offline, have called for Umar Khalid to be freed.

Titled “‘Humanity is a privilege’: Umar Khalid on his six years in an Indian jail without trial”, The Guardian article was written by Hannah Ellis-Petersen, the publication’s Delhi correspondent who is known for her anti-India propaganda. In the article, she described Khalid as an activist, a left-wing rights campaigner and a fierce critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She claimed that he had become a symbol of the alleged weaponisation of the judicial system against government opponents.

In a recent interview with Samdish Bhatia on Unfiltered by Samdish, Dipke claimed that he had kept his movement peaceful, Constitution-centric and difficult to discredit. Out of no where, Samdish remarked that his surname was not Khalid, to which Dipke said that had he been a Khalid, Saifi or Muslim, he would have been in jail. Through the remark, Dipke appeared to suggest that so-called Muslim “activists” such as Umar Khalid were imprisoned because of their religious identity, conveniently ignoring the serious criminal and conspiracy charges against them. The forceful insertion of Khalid’s reference was uncanny but gave the idea what exactly they were trying to do.

Spokesperson Saurav Das went further, describing the charges against Khalid as “false” and “frivolous” and calling his imprisonment a blot on India’s judiciary.

Another CJP spokesperson, Vijeta Dahiya, attempted to reduce the case against Khalid to a speech quoting Mahatma Gandhi and his presence in a WhatsApp group. When questioned about the larger conspiracy case and the more than 50 people killed during the Delhi Riots, Dahiya fell back on the argument that no trial had taken place and accused the journalist questioning him of being “godi media”.

body:
The argument was framed as a defence of due process. Let the trial happen, punish him if he is guilty and release him if he is innocent. However, the same people repeatedly cited the absence of a conviction as proof that the charges were false. They simultaneously demanded that the court process be allowed to conclude and treated the fact that it had not concluded as a declaration of innocence.

The procedural history was also more complicated than the slogan “six years without trial” suggested. Khalid’s latest plea, which was submitted to the court on 6th June, the same day CJP launched its first protest in Delhi, identified itself as his third bail application. His first and second bail applications were dismissed, as were subsequent appeals before the Delhi High Court. His Special Leave Petition was dismissed by the Supreme Court in January 2026, followed by the dismissal of his review petition in April.

The application itself reproduced the Supreme Court’s observation that the case involved several accused persons, voluminous documentary and electronic evidence and accusations concerning a structured and continuing conspiracy. The court also said the record did not show that Umar Khalid and the other accused were in jail only because of prosecution delays or that they had played no role in causing those delays.

While a debate over prolonged pre-trial detention is legitimate in a broader context, in Umar Khalid’s case, the delay in the trial was not caused by the justice system but by the accused themselves. Umar Khalid and the other accused in the larger conspiracy case used every possible tactic to delay the trial and then used the delay as an excuse to seek bail. From repeated bail pleas to pleas seeking to prevent the trial from starting, there was enough evidence to show that India’s justice system was not the culprit behind the six-year-long delay in the trial.

CJP Protestors Called Umar Khalid Their Leader

Support for Khalid was also visible at CJP’s first major protest at Jantar Mantar on 6th June. One protester was filmed declaring, “Umar Khalid is our leader.” Another said that he supported Khalid and saw nothing wrong with doing so. A CJP supporter also described Khalid and Sharjeel Imam as potential future occupants of the country’s highest political offices.

Did Abhijeet Dipke use Sonam Wangchuk?

> Abhijeet Dipke formed the CJP.
> Campaigned against the NEET paper leak and Dharmendra Pradhan on social media.
> Gained millions of followers on Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter within a few days.
> On June 6th, he came to India (Delhi) from us. He protested at Jantar Mantar, Delhi.
> After that, he protested in Pune, Bangalore, Amritsar, Lucknow, and Raipur.
> Involved Prakash Raj, Sonam Wangchuk, and other journalists, professors, and activists in his movement.
> Started an indefinite sit-in at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, on June 20th.
> When the government and the people ignored him, he asked Sonam Wangchuk to go on a hunger strike. @abhijeet_dipke should have done this himself.
> Today is the 12th day of Wangchuk's strike, but the Cockroach Janta Party's protest isn't having any visible impact. The people coming to Jantar Mantar in Delhi have no connection to this protest. They're simply coming there for food and drink. This is why the Cockroach Janta Party hasn't succeeded in its work yet.
> Slowly, Sonam Wangchuk is realizing that the CJP has used him for its own benefit. But it's too late; he can neither end his hunger strike nor retreat from Jantar Mantar in Delhi.

The bottom line is that just as Arvind Kejriwal did to Anna Hazare, Abhijeet Dipke is doing the same to Sonam Wangchuk.

Abhijeet Dipke's true agenda at Jantar Mantar stands exposed.

Far from championing NEET aspirants or genuine student grievances, Dipke exploited the paper leak outrage as a convenient pretext to orchestrate chaos and drama under the guise of protest. 

His so-called movement wasn't about securing justice for hardworking students—it was a calculated bid to stir unrest, draw media attention, and advance his own political theatre with the Cockroach Janta Party. 

While real victims of exam irregularities deserved focused advocacy, Dipke turned the site into a stage for overnight sit-ins, emotional appeals, and staged confrontations, prioritizing spectacle over solutions. 

This wasn't student solidarity; it was opportunism dressed up as activism, undermining the very cause it claimed to support.

Similarly, he joined the protests of the cockroach Janta Party, which was right, because no one wants any kind of compromise with the future of children.

**Fact check:** Mostly interpretive opinion with some facts.

Sonam Wangchuk joined the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP, satirical youth group founded by Abhijeet Dipke) protest at Jantar Mantar ~June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike. Demands: Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over alleged NEET-UG 2026 irregularities (re-exam was held) + Ladakh issues.

His prior Ladakh environmental fasts had wider support. Joining a direct anti-govt protest has polarized opinions — common when activism turns explicitly political.

“Pradhan responsible” is an allegation/demand, not proven fact. Protests focus on accountability so far; medical checks ongoing (per image). No major reported police clash or deliberate “sidelining” of NEET.

CJP mixes satire, youth anger, and serious demands. Perceptions shift when figures like Wangchuk broaden causes. Serious exam issues exist and need transparent probes.

This isn’t some harmless sit-down at Jantar Mantar anymore. The infection is spreading.

What began as the “Cockroach Janta Party” meme born from a CJI remark and weaponised on social media. It found its breeding ground in the NEET paper leak. 

Genuine NEET aspirants? Completely absent. The exams were conducted, their concerns addressed, yet these cockroaches refuse to leave. 

Why? Because they never gave a damn about NEET or students. This was always CAA 2.0. The same ugly, separatist, communal face now hidden under fresh makeup.

And the contagion has already reached the Supreme Court. We saw it with our own eyes when a young man stood there and hurled abuses. This is no longer protest. This is a deliberate, organised attempt to radicalise every disgruntled and dissatisfied youth, turn them against the country, against our institutions, and against India itself.

The slow poison is working. Time to call it what it is.
@rahulroushan nailed it.

**Analysis of HCP_2026 profile:**

- Bio & branding: "HIT Cockroach Janta Party", "cockroach mukt bharat 🪳" – satirical/troll style mocking the real "Cockroach Janta Party" (CJP) led by Abhijeet Dipke.
- Content pattern: Consistently criticizes CJP/anti-govt protests at Jantar Mantar, labels participants "leftists", "aandolanjeevi", "toolkit gang". Questions motives, accuses selective outrage vs NEET aspirants, mocks victim card & hunger strike claims. Defends against "dictatorship" narrative targeting Modi/BJP.

body:
The lukewarm response that the Cockroach Janta Party founders are witnessing at Jantar Mantar are the signs of the times we live in. Maasive following on Insta and Fb does not translate into on ground support. The generation which follows you on social media, especially the one's born post 2000, will not be willing to hit the streets. Heck, they are not even willing to walk down the road to get their daily household needs, because Blinkit, Zomato, Swiggy and their fourth friend Amazon, are all there, at their service. 

If only Urban Company and Pronto had an option, where one could hire protestors on one's behalf to protest for a cause, then the dwindling prospects of Cockroach Janta Party would have got a massive boost, but as of now, that functionality is not provided, but you never know.

Second, the faces of this movement lack charisma and public connect. Abhijeet Dipke is no mass leader, like Arvind Kejriwal, his persona and his background does not make the person behind the screen go like 'Woah, he is the guy I am willing to take 1 day off from my office'. 

Saurav Das and the other fellow, who keeps dancing to songs of 1990's Bollywood are not even Twitter celebrities. Also why would the generation following them, born post 2000, vibe to songs of Bollywood movies of 90's and the era of 2000 to 2010.

I did enjoy their dance performance, but then I am not your target audience. Similarly for all of Sonam Wangchuk's achievements, he too is no Anna Hazare and India of 2026, is not India of 2012. Life in India has become more comfortable, while the income disparity remains, both these truths run parallel. 

The issue of NEET, Ethanol are the one's which the ruling government should be rightly questioned about and one can even see supporters of the current government taking them to task on these 2 major issues.

However, the fast unto death emotional blackmail type of protest is passe. It no longer appeals to the current generation, neither to the one's previous to them, who actually grew up watching such protests overturn governments of the day.

A few days back, came across a clip of my friend @Iyervval where he spoke about how we don't realize that how far India has come from the days of abject poverty and this is where the answer to the lack of response to CJP's Dharna Party lies.

More than anything else, it is the lack of imagination on behalf of CJP, and taking a traditional route, which finds itself a lost child in today's comfort at the drop of an app button playstore.

Meanwhile, it is activist and News influencer @tehseenp 's campaign highlighting the issue of Ethanol that is drawing more attention, where in the elected representatives of the day,are being grudingly forced to acknowledge the issue.

May be, just may be, CJP folks study what AIM and Tehseen are saying and take a leaf out of their book.

2026 is not 2012!

Despite the 17 days Hunger Strike, the Government has not responded or opened any channels for dialogue between the two sides.

The plea urges authorities to shift him to a hospital and administer nutrition if necessary, citing concerns over his deteriorating health.

Wangchuk has been protesting at Delhi's Jantar Mantar as part of a campaign led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over NEET-UG paper leak. According to the petition, his worsening condition warrants urgent action to prevent a potentially tragic outcome.

Is the CJP now on its last legs?

Yes, the way HM Amit Shah and PM Modi test the patience of others is truly incredible.

1 = Their patience exposes the true face of their opponents.

2 = They put an end to anyone's political ambitions before they can achieve them.

3 = From the opposition to the leading political analysts, everyone agrees that HM Amit Shah is the Chanakya of modern politics.

Abhijeet Dipke also came to India from the US with the expectation that he would be arrested at Delhi Airport and that he would play the victim card, garner sympathy from the people of the country, and enter politics.

And here, everything happened exactly the opposite: no arrests, no debate, but instead, a protest was allowed at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, without Delhi Police permission.

 As the days passed, the true face of the Cockroach Janta Party began to be revealed. The arrival of all the opposition political parties, leftists, NGOs, and organizations at Jantar Mantar in Delhi is weakening the CJP. This is causing it to lose its popularity among the common people.

At the same time, the popularity and trust of the BJP and PM Modi is increasing among the people. Among the people CJP provides a platform to, there are some whose ideology and agenda people do not agree with at all.

This is why, even after Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike, Abhijeet Dipke is still not receiving public support; instead, people are creating and sharing memes about him.

Now Abhijeet Dipke is meeting everyone whom the people of the country have already rejected. No one listens to him, and no one follows him.

body:
I want to take a moment to thank Abhijeet Dipke.
For 19 days now, he has been teaching this nation a masterclass.

Not in exam reform.
In something more valuable.

He flew in from Boston. Unemployed.
To save India's students.

Then handed the mic to Allah.
Kashmir.
RSS.
Umar Khalid.

Wait.
Where is Dharmendra Pradhan?

Well. 
He is not generating any TRP.
And he is having fun continuing as Education Minister.

Turns out the fastest way to save a minister's job is to hire professional protestors.

Pradhan should be sending flowers to Jantar Mantar.
Maybe Pradhan hired Abhijeet Dipke.

Nobody even remembers his name is on the placards anymore.

Special mention to Sonam Wangchuk.
Came for a guest appearance.
Stayed to become the whole show.

19 days without food. Visibly.
While everyone else on that stage eats on schedule.

And the menu is incredible.

Continental on Monday.
Chinese on Tuesday.
Hyderabadi on Wednesday.
American on Thursday.
Repeat.

With desserts.
Tea.
Coffee.

Imagine fasting for 19 days next to a buffet you're not invited to.

Every speaker walks up.
Says a few lines about Allah.
Ambedkar.
Kashmir.
RSS.
Umar Khalid.
Then walks off to eat.

Wangchuk stays.
Hungry.
Foolish.
Watching.

Wondering if anyone even remembers what this started as.
At some point even the most patient man starts doing math.

If Wangchuk could speak freely right now. 
Off the record.
We suspect it would not be about the education ministry.
It would be about catering.

Here's the real service Dipke has done this country.
He has finally taught us how to spot a cockroach.

Not the ones NEET aspirants are competing against for a medical seat.
The ones standing on a stage at Jantar Mantar.

Holding a mic.
Talking about everything except the paper leak that started this.
And still don't know who is President of India.

The real students are indoors.
Revising.
Silent.
Unheard.
The stage belongs to everyone else now.

So thank you, Abhijeet Dipke.
You didn't get Pradhan to resign.
You got India to forget why he should.

That takes talent.

Popularity isn't evidence, and dissent isn't immunity. 

My point was never that people can't protest, it's that the conversation has shifted from the students who were wronged to the personality leading the headlines. 

That's political theatre, not accountability, Dr. Sharma. Everyone knows why CJP was formed, why it occupied Jantar Mantar, and the kind of slogans that echoed there.

No one is disregarding the real anguish of the NEET aspirants and families whose years of hard work were destroyed by this leak and the authorities' repeated failures. But they deserve more than this activist led spectacle. 

Rather than this Wangchuk, more of the people must come out and protest.
empty fasts and selective outrage won't deliver that.

The post shares a critical graphic about the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

**Background:** CJP (founded by Abhijeet Dipke as satire after a CJI “cockroach” remark) led protests over NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks, exam irregularities, student stress & suicides. Main demands: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation + accountability.

It drew opposition support & attention. However, clips from the protest include political slogans (anti-BJP/RSS), “Allah ka nare”, remarks questioning “Maharaj” titles & Sanatan traditions, plus lines like “Mera Ling Meri Marzi”.

**The debate:** Did unrelated politics & religious commentary hijack a student education protest? Or is it valid broader dissent?

Core student issues (leaks, fairness) remain real — mixing agendas often fractures focus & support. What do you think?

body: कायदे से उन ऐंकरों को जाना चाहिए था, जिनसे चैनल की पहचान है। अच्छा है इसी बहाने नए चेहरों को मौक़ा मिल जाता है। ऐसा लगता है कि संवाददाता से अनजाने में यह बात निकल गई होगी, क्योंकि 2014 के बाद से यही पैटर्न बना दिया गया है। धरना प्रदर्शन को सीधे देश विरोधी साज़िश से जोड़ दिया जाता है और नारों से डराया जाने लगता है। इसी का इतना भय हो गया है कि धरना प्रदर्शन के पहले ही लोग कहने लगते हैं कि विपक्ष से हम दूर हैं। यह समस्या कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी की नहीं, महिला कुश्ती खिलाड़ियों की भी थी, शायद उससे पहले किसान आंदोलन की। इस बार एक चेंज दिख रहा है। विपक्ष और धरना प्रदर्शन को लेकर झिझक टूटने लगी है। कई दल गए हैं। कांग्रेस ने भी नैतिक समर्थन दे दिया है। गोदी मीडिया यहाँ से क्या करेगा? कांग्रेस के समर्थन के बाद इस अनशन को मोदी के ख़िलाफ बड़ी साज़िश बताने लग जाएगा या मोदी सरकार से सवाल करेगा। अभिजीत ने पहले जो भी कहा हो मगर राहुल गांधी के सवाल को कैसे हैंडल करना है, यह बात अब समझने लगे हैं। इसीलिए नए लोगों से ख़ूब सवाल होने चाहिए। कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी से यह सवाल नहीं होता तो यह बदलाव नहीं आता। जनता की निगाह में आना, उसके भरोसे पर उतरना आसान काम नहीं है।

Police came in civil dress, beat students at Jantar Mantar & abducted Sonam Sir.

One of the protestors says, "Early in the morning, they sent in about ten police officers, claiming they were a medical team. We realized they were police since they didn't look like doctors and they ordered all the volunteers to move aside. We kept requesting them to wait, but suddenly they announced that there was a High Court order requiring them to take Sonam Sir away. Meanwhile, Abhijit had just went away to use the restroom; I believe they have arrested him too which is why he cannot come here, and his phone isn't connecting either...All the policemen were in plain clothes..."

Can U believe it? 'Op Nalla' just took 30 seconds? In 30 seconds, .@AmitShah Ji & Delhi Police Commissioner wound up months-old plan of burning Bharat 😂

Reportedly-
👉At 3 am Saturday—almost 4 hrs before Nalla Sonam was picked up like a stray dog from the Jantar Mantar protest site by Delhi Police—all personnel of New Delhi district police assembled.
👉They were told it's for a security drill in Parliament before the Monsoon Session.
👉Then they were taken to Mandir Marg police station, where they were informed that Operation is to remove Nalla Sonam from Jantar Mantar within “30 seconds”.
👉One team was stationed outside the flat where Abhijeet Dipke goes to have rangraliyan every night.
👉Minutes before Wangchuk’s removal, the police installed a phone jammer in the area.
👉Around 6.30 am, they quickly placed a white curtain across the stage and removed Nalla—before anyone could see what was going on behind the curtain.
👉Nalla was zapped. Cockroach Dipke was shocked to see police outside his 'night hideout'. Expected Delhi Police to arrest him. Instead, Police dropped him at Jantar Mantar to replace one stray dog with other. All efforts to create tension defused in one instance.

Choosing right man for the right post is most important job for a Minister. Mota Bhai proved it by appointing Anurag Kumar (with IB experience) for the post & he delivered perfectly.... In just 30 seconds.

शिक्षा मंत्री Dharmendra Pradhan को इस्तीफ़ा देना चाहिए।

PUBLIC ADVISORY 

In view of reports of a proposed march to Parliament by CJP on 20.07.2026 (Monday), Delhi Police hereby categorically clarifies  that no permission has been sought or granted for any such protest march/procession.

Prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS (erstwhile section 144 CrPC) is in force in the New Delhi District. *Accordingly, protest marches, processions, demonstrations and assemblies of five or more persons are strictly prohibited*, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar,  with prior permission.

As Parliament session is commencing from 20 July, strict security arrangements are in place to ensure public safety, security of protectees, and the protection of vital government installations.

Any person violating these prohibitory orders shall be liable for prosecution under Section 223 BNS and other applicable provisions of law.

Delhi Police appeals to all citizens to respect the law, refrain from participating in any unauthorised gathering or march, and cooperate in maintaining public peace, safety and security.

VIDEO | DCP New Delhi, Sachin Sharma clarifies that no application seeking permission for a march by CJP has been received by the Delhi Police, nor has any permission been granted. 

He says, "In view of reports about a proposed march to Parliament by the Cockroach Janta Party on July 20, it is categorically clarified that no application seeking permission for such a march has been received by the Delhi Police, nor has any permission been granted. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) are in force across the entire New Delhi district. Accordingly, the assembly of five or more persons, protest marches, or demonstrations are prohibited, except at the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar, and that too only with prior permission. The Parliament session is also commencing tomorrow. Therefore, elaborate security arrangements will be in place to ensure public safety, security, and the protection of vital government installations. Any person found violating the orders issued under Section 163 of the BNSS will be liable for legal action. Delhi Police appeals to all citizens to respect the law, refrain from participating in any unauthorised gatherings or marches, and cooperate in maintaining public peace and safety."

(Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)

body: #WATCH | Delhi | On CJP protest, Congress MP Shashi Tharoor says, "When a non-violent protest is taking place, what is the reason for a lathi-charge? Lathi charge is not an act of non-violence. It is an act of violence. I don't understand the logic of this.  Similarly here in Parliament,  everyone knows these are burning issues across the country.  It would be logical to have a discussion on them. Parliament is supposed to be the place where we can ventilate the voice of the people, the concerns of the people.  Once we do that,  we all know the government has a majority. As the old saying goes, the Opposition must have its say because the government will have its way. They have the majority. But at least let parliament be a forum where these concerns can be heard, can be truly ventilated and voiced, where various people can represent the views of their constituents.  Then the government can disagree. But right now, just refusing a discussion is what has led to today's disruption because the opposition wanted these issues up there, wanted an opportunity to talk about them on the floor of the house. If Parliament is not for raising these issues,  then honestly, what is it for? I mean, it can't just be a sort of notice board for the government to announce its bills and get them passed with a rubber stamp. That's not what Parliament is all about. It should be a forum where all these views can be heard, discussed, debated as necessary and then passed. The Prime Minister has sought cooperation from the opposition. We'll cooperate if they cooperate. The idea should be that there should be mutual cooperation. Let them permit certain discussions. This has got to be give and take. That's the way Parliament is supposed to function."

The government met members of the satirical political group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) after they held a protest in central Delhi today, sources said. The CJP has been demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak.

The group's spokesperson @SauravDassss in a post on X said that he and another spokesperson, @AshutoshRanka, met Union minister JP Nadda at his house for 10 minutes.

"While we submit a written letter with our demands, he has assured us that he will meanwhile speak internally. We are in that process..." Das said. "The minister assured us he will discuss this at the appropriate level. However, no commitments have been made so far. The peaceful protesters will not rest until the demand is met."

He also shared a copy of the letter on X.

Heart goes out to NEET Aspirants across India who feel cheated and want transparency and accountability. 

But many genuine students participating in the protest and raising their demands may not realize that Sonam Wangchuk and Abhijeet Dipke are not sacrificing or working solely for the interests of students. Their objective is something else.

By involving people whom many consider to be anti-Hindu forces or those associated with the "Bharat tere tukde honge" slogan, these protests can no longer be said to represent only students' concerns.

Arundhati Roy has repeatedly stated that Kashmir is not a part of India and that the Indian Army has forcibly occupied it. If you organize a protest with the support of such individuals, majority of the people will not support your cause.

Shabana Azmi also appeared at Jantar Mantar, is associated with Christian NGOs whose objective is to convert Hindus. Slogans such as "Naam Rahega Allah Ka" are also being raised.

If such activities are intended to create unrest or disorder in the country, then, in my view, any action taken by the administration or the police including the lawful use of force to protect India's integrity would be justified.
